script.cite: BK2 printed p.7 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.13, rule 'the number being remembered corresponds with the section (1-6) which has a relay light ON'; derived from topology, not printed: pushbutton 5 down put + on the wiper (6+/6Z-6Y(pb6 up)/5X-5Y/D16) and the hand at D4 fed D4/4G/4C-lamp-4E-coil-4F/4-, so relay 4 pulled in; its set-1 arm 4H (strapped to + through the 1H..5H/6Y chain and pushbutton 6's N.C. contact) now makes 4G and holds the coil and light after pushbutton 5 is released; every other pad is dead (wiper off it, pushbutton 5 up, G contacts open), relay 6's coil and lamp (6C/6E/6F) are unwired, so the other relays stay out and their lights off
script.quote: This experiment demonstrates how MINIVAC 601 may receive decimal input data and instructions. A decimal number is communicated to the computer by turning the DECIMAL INPUT-OUTPUT knob to the desired number and pushing pushbutton 5 to instruct the computer to remember the selected number. Another instruction—to forget all previous data—is given to the computer by pushing pushbutton 6. [...] With decimal data, the number being remembered corresponds with the section (1-6) which has a relay light ON.

script.cite: BK2 printed p.7 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.13, rule 'the number being remembered corresponds with the section (1-6) which has a relay light ON'; derived from topology, not printed: pushbutton 6 down opened 6Y-6Z, the only + feed to the arms 1H..5H, so the holding relay (relay 4) dropped; after release 6Y is back on +, but every G contact is open again and pushbutton 5 is up, so no coil is fed: all relays out, all relay lights off

note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the 23-wire topology and the p.7 rule, not printed. Topology: pushbutton 6's N.C. contact (6Z/6+) puts + on 6Y, which feeds both the set-1 arms 1H..5H (chained 1H/2H..4H/5H, 5H/6Y) and pushbutton 5's N.O. contact (6Y/5X); pushbutton 5's arm drives the wiper (5Y/D16). Pad DN joins relay N's N.O. contact NG and the far side of its indicator lamp NC; the coil returns NF to minus. Pushbutton 5 down with the hand at N pulls relay N in through its light; NH-NG then latches it from + until pushbutton 6 opens 6Y-6Z. Script: printed step 1 (knob to 4, pushbutton 5) and step 2 (pushbutton 6 and release), then the step-2 reader-chosen digit run for each of 1, 2, 3 and 5, clearing with pushbutton 6 before each turn of the knob so every pad is dead while the wiper sweeps (no reliance on how the wiper crosses pads). Asserted: relay N in and light N on with every other relay out and light off after each store (Step 7 notes, II-EXP2), and all relays out and lights off after pushbutton 6. Not asserted: digit 0 or 6 and above (the page offers 1-5 only), a second digit stored on top of the first, and anything while a button is held. Pushbuttons are pressed and released as separate steps; the knob is turned by dialGrab at 22.5 degrees per pad, as in C1/II-EXP2.
